title: What does @Transactional(readOnly=true) optimize, how does it relate to dirty checking, and why is Open Session In View an anti-pattern?
topicTitle: Performance: Large IN, Dirty Checking, OSIV
keyPoints: @Transactional(readOnly=true) sets FlushMode to MANUAL, skipping dirty checking entirely for that transaction.
Dirty checking compares every managed entity's current state against a snapshot taken at load time, which is wasted CPU on pure reads.
The readOnly flag also sets the JDBC connection read-only, enabling replica routing and relaxed locking on supported databases.
OSIV (Open Session In View) keeps the Hibernate Session open for the entire HTTP request, hiding N+1 queries and holding connections too long.
Disable OSIV with spring.jpa.open-in-view=false and fetch everything inside the service transaction using JOIN FETCH or DTO projections.
Combining readOnly=true with DTO projections gives the best read performance because neither dirty checking nor entity snapshots occur.

s1_definition.oneliner: readOnly=true skips dirty checking and enables replica reads; OSIV keeps the session open too long and hides N+1 queries, so disable it.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **@Transactional(readOnly=true)** – hints that the transaction performs no writes, so Hibernate sets FlushMode to MANUAL and skips dirty-check snapshot comparisons.
- **Dirty checking** – the process where Hibernate compares every managed entity's current state against a snapshot taken at load time to generate UPDATE statements at flush.
- **FlushMode.MANUAL** – prevents automatic flushing, so no dirty-check comparison runs and accidental mutations are never persisted.
- **JDBC read-only connection** – the readOnly flag sets the connection to read-only, allowing the database driver or pool to route queries to a read replica.
- **Open Session In View (OSIV)** – a Spring Boot default (spring.jpa.open-in-view=true) that binds the Hibernate Session to the entire HTTP request so lazy associations can load in the controller or view layer.
- **OSIV downsides** – holds database connections longer, hides N+1 queries fired from the view layer, and blurs transaction boundaries.
s1_definition.analogy: readOnly=true is like telling the bank clerk at National Bank of India that you are only here to check your balance, not to make any changes. The clerk skips the slow double-checking of whether anything was edited (dirty checking) and can send you to a faster viewing-only counter (a read replica). OSIV is like leaving the vault door open for your entire visit so you can keep fetching more files whenever you remember them. It is convenient, but it ties up the vault and the clerk far too long, and you never notice you are making a hundred trips instead of one.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Dirty Checking Flow (writable transaction)
  ============================================

  persist(account)     load(account)       flush / commit
       |                    |                    |
       v                    v                    v
  +-----------+      +-------------+      +------------------+
  | Entity    |      | Entity      |      | For EACH entity: |
  | created   |----->| snapshot[]  |----->| current == snap? |
  |           |      | stored in   |      | YES -> skip      |
  |           |      | Persistence |      | NO  -> UPDATE    |
  +-----------+      | Context     |      +------------------+
                     +-------------+

  readOnly=true: FlushMode = MANUAL
  ============================================

  persist(account)     load(account)       commit
       |                    |                 |
       v                    v                 v
  +-----------+      +-------------+      +----------+
  | Entity    |      | NO snapshot |      | No flush |
  | created   |----->| stored      |----->| No check |
  |           |      |             |      | Fast     |
  +-----------+      +-------------+      +----------+

  OSIV Connection Timeline
  ============================================

  OSIV ON:
  |-- Request --|-- Service --|-- Controller --|-- JSON --|-- Response --|
  |<============ Connection held entire request ========================>|

  OSIV OFF:
  |-- Request --|-- Service --|-- Controller --|-- JSON --|-- Response --|
                |<= Conn held =>|
                   (released)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
The readOnly flag on @Transactional is both a performance optimization and a safety guard. When Rajesh marks a balance-enquiry method readOnly=true in the National Bank of India service, Hibernate sets the flush mode to manual, which means it skips dirty checking entirely. Normally Hibernate snapshots every loaded entity and, at flush time, compares the current state to the snapshot to generate updates. For a pure read that comparison is wasted CPU, and skipping it saves memory and time. The JDBC connection is also flagged read-only, which the database driver or pool can use to route the query to a read replica.

Open Session In View is the anti-pattern that Pankaj, the architect, disables in every microservice at National Bank of India. With OSIV on, Spring binds the Hibernate session to the whole HTTP request, so lazy associations can load anywhere, even during JSON serialization. That convenience hides three real problems: the database connection is held for the entire request duration, lazy loads in the controller fire invisible N+1 queries, and the transaction boundary no longer maps to the service method. Disabling OSIV with spring.jpa.open-in-view=false forces the team to fetch everything inside the service transaction using JOIN FETCH or DTO projections, which makes the query count explicit and predictable.

The senior position is that readOnly=true on every read method, OSIV disabled, and DTO projections for list endpoints together give the fastest, most predictable read path. Connections are released promptly, dirty checking is eliminated, and N+1 queries are impossible because lazy loads outside the session throw a LazyInitializationException that forces the developer to fix the fetch strategy rather than hide it.

Remember one sentence: readOnly=true skips dirty checking and enables replica routing, while OSIV disabled forces explicit fetch strategies and releases connections promptly.
